slander.label: Slander
slander.description: {victim} tells anyone who will listen that {perpetrator} is a coward and a cheat ({location})

merchant_slander.label: Merchant Slander
merchant_slander.description: {victim} warn the market that {perpetrator}'s company pays late and sells short weight ({location})

contract_broken.label: Broken Contract
contract_broken.description: {perpetrator} promised {victim} goods for {location} and never delivered

massacre.label: Massacre
massacre.description: {perpetrator} took the surrender of {location} and then put it to the sword

hostages_hanged.label: Hostages Hanged
hostages_hanged.description: {perpetrator} hanged hostages before the walls of {location}

fields_salted.label: Fields Salted
fields_salted.description: {perpetrator} sowed the fields of {location} with salt

plague_flung.label: Plague Dead Flung
plague_flung.description: {perpetrator} flung the plague dead over the walls of {location}

famine_dole.label: Famine Dole
famine_dole.description: {perpetrator} fed the hungry of {location} from their own treasury

feast_given.label: A Feast
feast_given.description: {perpetrator} kept a feast at {location} that the guests are still talking about

pilgrimage_made.label: Pilgrimage
pilgrimage_made.description: {perpetrator} walked the pilgrim's road and knelt at {location}

feast_brawl.label: Brawl at a Feast
feast_brawl.description: there was a brawl at {perpetrator}'s table in {location}, and the host was in the thick of it

beast_slain.label: Beast Slain
beast_slain.description: {perpetrator} faced down {victim} in the wilds near {location}

wilds_rescue.label: Rescue in the Wilds
wilds_rescue.description: {perpetrator} saved {victim} out in the wilds near {location}

wilds_find.label: A Find in the Wilds
wilds_find.description: {perpetrator} came back from the wilds near {location} with {victim}

affair.label: Affair
affair.description: {perpetrator} has been seen keeping close company with {victim} of {location}, and {perpetrator} a married soul

mail_opened.label: Broken Seals
mail_opened.description: {perpetrator} has been reading other people's letters: the seal of {victim} was found lifted in {location}

letter_aloud.label: Read Aloud
letter_aloud._note: A letter of the player's to one who cannot read, read out to them by a neighbour or the priest, who told what was in it (systems/literacy.js afterAloud)
letter_aloud.description: {perpetrator} wrote to {victim} of {location}, who cannot read: whoever read it out has told the whole street what was in it

boast.label: Tall Talk
boast._note: What the player told a townsperson about themselves in free talk, and asked them to pass on (systems/npcChatImpact.js spread_word): idle talk, no penalty. {victim} is the claim.

well_poisoning.label: Well Poisoner
well_poisoning._note: A town's well poisoned (systems/townCrimes.js), the culprit named by a witness.
well_poisoning.description: {perpetrator} poisoned the well of {location}, and {victim} drank of it

granary_arson.label: Granary Burner
granary_arson._note: A town's granary burnt (systems/townCrimes.js), the culprit named by a witness.
granary_arson.description: {perpetrator} burnt the granary of {location} and left {victim} to go hungry

plague_lie.label: Plague Liar
plague_lie._note: A false plague scare (systems/townCrimes.js) traced to the player, or the player seen paying the criers.
plague_lie.description: {perpetrator} cried plague on {location} for profit, and {victim} paid for it

whisperer.label: Whisperer Exposed
whisperer.description: {perpetrator} was the one spreading those lies about {victim}, it's been traced back to {location}

desecration.label: Crypt Desecrated
desecration._note: The player seen breaking a rival House's crypt (systems/profaneCrimes.js, Gossip.accuse). {victim} is the House.
desecration.description: {perpetrator} broke open the crypt of {victim} at {location} and scattered their dead

relic_fraud.label: False Relic
relic_fraud._note: A fake relic the player sold to a temple, found out (systems/profaneCrimes.js). {victim} is the relic.
relic_fraud.description: {perpetrator} sold the temple at {location} {victim}, and it was pig bones in a gilt box

relic_betrayal.label: Relic Sold to Heretics
relic_betrayal._note: A true relic of the player's own faith sold to another (systems/profaneCrimes.js). {victim} is the relic.
relic_betrayal.description: {perpetrator} sold {victim} to the priests of another god at {location}

false_witch.label: False Accuser
false_witch._note: The player cried witch and the trial acquitted her, or a mob burned her (systems/profaneCrimes.js). {victim} is the accused.
false_witch.description: {perpetrator} cried witch on {victim} at {location}, and folk say it was for her land

blackmailer.label: Blackmail
blackmailer.description: {perpetrator} tried to blackmail {victim}, and the crown's men know it ({location})

vanished_talk.label: Gone Missing
vanished_talk._note: A townsperson who left with the player and never came home (systems/vanishings.js, the doubt tier): talk, no penalty. {victim} is the one lost.
vanished_talk.description: {victim} of {location} took the road with {perpetrator} and never came home, folk say

vanished_companion.label: Foul Play Suspected
vanished_companion._note: A companion lost with the player in a way that looks like foul play (systems/vanishings.js, the foul tier, Gossip.accuse); credibility from the suspicion. Grown in the telling it can turn the watch.
vanished_companion.description: {victim} of {location} took the road with {perpetrator} and was never seen again, and folk say it was no accident

tellings._comment: Rumours grow in the telling. Each time a rumour reaches a new town, the teller either passes on the version they heard (inherit) or changes it (chance). A telling multiplies the rumour's severity in that town (consequences, guard hostility) and replaces its text there. {base} is the plain description; {perpetrator} {victim} {location} {rival} fill as usual. 'stolen' deeds are credited to someone else; 'clears' tellings no longer name the player.

crime.label: Grown in the telling
crime.text: {base}. And two more who tried to stop it, the way it's told here.

crime.label: Monstrous
crime.text: They say {perpetrator} did unspeakable things to {victim} in {location}. Some swear there was a black rite in it.

crime.label: Softened
crime.text: Word is {perpetrator} and {victim} fell to blows in {location}. Who started it depends on who's telling.

crime.label: Blamed on a stranger
crime.text: Something ugly happened to {victim} in {location}. A stranger in a grey cloak, most say. Nobody here names {perpetrator}.

crime.label: Garbled
crime.text: {perpetrator}, or someone with a name like it, did for {victim} somewhere past {location}. Or was it the other way round?

deed.label: Become legend
deed.text: {base}. Single-handed, if you believe the telling here, and laughing the while.

deed.label: Credited to another
deed.text: {base}... except here they swear it was {rival}, not {perpetrator}.

deed.label: Soured
deed.text: {base}, they say, though some whisper it was done for gain, not goodness.

talk.label: Grown in the telling
talk.text: {perpetrator} and {victim} of {location}! Caught in the hayloft, they say, and not for the first time.

talk.label: Doubted
talk.text: Some say {perpetrator} is sweet on {victim} of {location}. Others say that's the ale talking.

refuted.label: Sung down
refuted.text: There's a song going round that {perpetrator} was falsely accused over {victim}. The bard tells it well.

deedRenown._comment: A deed's word is worth deedWeight = local severity / refSeverity x the telling's regard (legend 1.2, soured 0.3, stolen 0), clamped to [minWeight, maxWeight]. Each town it reaches raises the player's reputation with that town's realm by reputationPerTown x weight (up to reputationCap); a friend there who hears it warms by matters.config.deedPraise x weight. A type with localRenown false (a sack) wins no realm's love.

scandals._comment: Court scandals (systems/whispers.js): tales about the great (rulers, rival adventurers) that hatch at a capital or a town, spread town to town, gather heat and weigh on the realm's stability (kingdom.scandal.stab, read by world/kingdomState.js). Some are true, some are lies; nobody knows which until it is proven, debunked or forgotten. The player hears them in taverns and can fan them, quash them, dig for the truth, blackmail the subject, sell the proof to an enemy crown, or plant a tale of their own. Lines: {subject} {place} {kingdom} {enemy}. fallout.proven / fallout.debunked: what a ruler's tale does to the realm on top of the stability shock (stability, unity, piety, treasuryPct, enemyRelations, advisorLoyalty — Whispers.applyFallout).

bastard.label: A Hidden Bastard
lines: They say {subject} has a bastard hidden away in {place}, and the child has the royal eyes.
A wet-nurse in {place} swears she suckled a child of {subject}'s. Paid in crown silver, she says.
bastard.proven: A child of {subject}'s, born on the wrong side of the blanket, was found in {place}. The court of {kingdom} is in uproar.
bastard.debunked: The so-called bastard of {subject} turned out to be a miller's boy with a lying mother. {subject} is vindicated.

poison.label: A Poisoning
lines: They say {subject}'s uncle didn't die of a fever. Something in the wine, from a cup {subject} poured.
A cook from the palace fled to {place}. She won't say what she put in the soup, or who told her to.
poison.proven: The palace cook confessed before the priests: {subject} ordered the poison. {kingdom} reels.
poison.debunked: The cook who 'fled' turned up drunk in a ditch and recanted everything. The tale of {subject}'s poison dies.

debts.label: The Crown's Debts
lines: They say {subject} has pawned the crown jewels to the moneylenders. Paste on the royal head, gold in a vault in {place}.
Soldiers in {kingdom} haven't seen silver in weeks. {subject} is broke, and everyone knows it but the heralds.
debts.proven: The moneylenders of {place} went public with the pawn tickets. {subject} is a debtor king, and {kingdom} knows it.
debts.debunked: {subject} paid the garrison in full, in good coin, in the square at {place}. So much for the debts.

heresy.label: A Secret Heresy
lines: They say {subject} keeps an old idol in a locked room and prays to it at night.
A chapel boy in {place} saw {subject} spit on the altar. Nobody believed him. Then he vanished.
heresy.proven: The idol was found, exactly where they said. The priests of {kingdom} turn their faces from {subject}.
heresy.debunked: {subject} walked barefoot to the shrine at {place} and was blessed before the crowd. The heresy talk withers.

pact.label: A Secret Pact
lines: They say {subject} writes secret letters to {enemy}. Our sons die so the crown can haggle over the peace.
A courier was stopped near {place} with {enemy}'s seal in his boot. They say the letter was for {subject}.
pact.proven: The letters were real. {subject} has been bargaining with {enemy} behind {kingdom}'s back.
pact.debunked: The 'letters to {enemy}' were forged by a clerk with a grudge. He hanged in {place} this morning.

coward.label: Cowardice
lines: They say {subject} ran from a fight near {place}, left their own people in the mud.
Ask anyone in {place}: {subject} hid in a wine cellar while better folk did the fighting.
coward.proven: Three survivors from {place} told it the same way: {subject} ran. The name won't wash clean.
coward.debunked: {subject} showed the scars from {place} in the square. Nobody calls them a coward now.

affair.label: An Affair
lines: They say {subject} slips out at night to a house in {place}, and it isn't to pray.
A maid in {place} found {subject}'s ring in a bed where it had no business being.
affair.proven: {subject} was caught leaving the house in {place} at dawn. The whole of {kingdom} is laughing.
affair.debunked: The house in {place} turned out to belong to {subject}'s old nurse. The affair talk sours into pity.

madness.label: Madness
lines: They say {subject} talks to the portraits now, and waits for them to answer.
A guard from the palace drinks in {place}. He says {subject} had the hounds tried for treason.
madness.proven: {subject} addressed the court of {kingdom} as if it were a flock of geese. The councillors exchange looks.
madness.debunked: {subject} held a sharp, cold council at {place} and dismissed the guard who'd talked. Mad as a fox, maybe.

cheat.label: A Cheat
lines: They say {subject} rigged the lists at {place}. Bribed the marshal, loosened a rival's girth.
{subject}'s loaded dice cleaned out half the soldiers in {place}, they say.
cheat.proven: The marshal of {place} confessed: {subject} paid him. The name is mud in every tavern.
cheat.debunked: The 'loaded dice' were checked by the priests of {place}: honest bone. {subject} is cleared.

graverobber.label: Grave-Robbing
lines: They say {subject} sells the bones out of the old tombs to the witches in {place}.
That gold {subject} spends so freely? Grave-goods. Someone's grandmother's rings, they say, from {place}.
graverobber.proven: A fence in {place} named {subject} as the source of the grave-goods. The priests want answers.
graverobber.debunked: The grave-goods were traced to a gang in {place}, not to {subject}. An apology is owed.
